sections.content:
15,800 people

were counted on the census as "other psychologists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Psychologists research, study and assess emotional, cognitive and behavioural processes and abnormalities in human beings and animals and how these are affected by genetic, physical and social factors.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "other psychologists" there were more women than men (83% compared with 17%).

This means "other psychologists" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 17% and women made up 83% of "other psychologists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other psychologists" included:

  • clinical psychologists
  • clothing, fashion and accessories designers
  • care workers and home carers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "other psychologists", 20.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other psychologists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other psychologists" included:

  • finance and investment analysts and advisers
  • optometrists
  • business sales executives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other psychologists", 10.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (68.2% compared with 31.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (79.1%) than self-employed (20.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
